source_name: Small/second-tier bank own vacancy pages (Bank Sich, Bank Portal)
why_relevant: Small banks rarely appear on IT boards; their own HR pages are the only place their IT/АБС/card-processing roles surface, and small banks are the most displaceable vendor accounts.

source_name: LinkedIn — Ukrainian bank company pages and banking job feed
why_relevant: Bank and processor LinkedIn pages (PrivatBank, OTP Bank Ukraine, UPC) publish senior/vendor-facing roles and employee-profile stack claims; ~233 banking jobs listed for Ukraine at time of search. Employee headline/skill fields are a secondary route to incumbent platform names.

source_name: CS Ltd (csltd.com.ua) — vendor site for CBS Б2, Ukraine's most-deployed core banking system
why_relevant: The vendor behind the 'АБС Б2' requirement that recurs in Ukrainian bank vacancies. Its product/module pages give the exact module vocabulary (deposits, integration, payment settlement centre) needed to parse vacancy texts and to map which bank runs which Б2 module set; it is also the key incumbent to displace.

source_name: OpenWay Group site + OpenWay recruitment posts (WAY4 platform)
source_subtype: vendor site / case studies + recruitment posts
why_relevant: WAY4 is the processing platform behind Oschadbank's own processing centre; OpenWay's own vacancy posts and case studies name deploying institutions, giving both the glossary term ('Way4', 'WAY4 Cards') to hunt in bank vacancies and the deployment map to corroborate hiring signals.

source_name: Jooble Ukraine — aggregated bank/IT vacancy index
why_relevant: Aggregates postings from boards and company ATSs into one searchable index (~900+ Kyiv bank vacancies observed), useful as a discovery layer to find employers and boards not yet on the actor map, then snowball to the primary posting.

source_name: Indeed Ukraine — bank vacancy index
why_relevant: Independent aggregation of Ukrainian bank vacancies (NBU and commercial banks) with different coverage from local boards; useful for cross-checking whether a hiring surge is real or a single-board artefact.

source_name: OLX.ua — jobs section (bank/service-technician roles)
why_relevant: Carries regional field-service and terminal/ATM technician vacancies from small integrators and outsourcers that never appear on IT boards — the layer that reveals who physically services which bank's hardware fleet in the regions.

source_name: Happy Monday — FinTech/Finance vacancy vertical
why_relevant: Curated UA career platform with a dedicated fintech category; captures product/engineering roles at PSPs and fintechs that skip the mass boards, plus editorial company profiles that describe stack and team structure.

source_name: Telegram vacancy channels for UA IT/fintech (via tgstat career directory)
why_relevant: A large share of Ukrainian IT and fintech vacancies circulate first (and sometimes only) in Telegram channels, often with fuller stack detail than the sanitised board version, and hours-to-days earlier. tgstat's career directory is the discovery layer for which channels to subscribe to.

source_name: Association of Ukrainian Banks (AUB) news — bank IT/platform announcements
why_relevant: Industry-association newswire that publishes bank technology milestones (e.g. Oschadbank launching its own WAY4-based processing centre). Serves as the corroboration layer that converts a hiring-signal hypothesis into a dated, attributable deployment fact.

source_name: YouControl — page listing its 220+ underlying data sources
why_relevant: A published inventory of the Ukrainian registries and datasets that aggregators consume. Effectively a ready-made map of upstream primary sources for the whole workstream — use it to discover registries this cell has not yet covered.

source_name: OpenDataBot API developer documentation
why_relevant: Technical contract for programmatic access — endpoints, fields and coverage for EDR, court register, debtors register and related datasets. Determines what can be collected at scale and at what granularity.

source_name: Opendatabot Court — Єдиний державний реєстр судових рішень (ЄДРСР) пошук
why_relevant: Searchable front-end over the unified court-decisions register. Litigation between a bank and a supplier is often the only public trace of a contract that was never announced — judgments frequently name contract numbers, equipment models and amounts.

source_name: Єдиний державний реєстр юридичних осіб, ФОП та громадських формувань (ЄДР) — Мін'юст
why_relevant: The primary registry every aggregator resells: legal name, EDRPOU, KVED activity codes, directors, founders/beneficiaries, capital, status. Authoritative ground truth for identifying and de-duplicating vendor entities before linking them to contracts.

source_name: VKURSI.PRO — перевірка компаній, ФОП і відкритих даних
why_relevant: Third major Ukrainian counterparty-intelligence platform (70+ sources): tender history by period, court decisions, sanctions, financial analytics, trademarks, plus a connection-finder linking companies by shared directors/founders/addresses. Segmentation by KVED and region makes it usable to build vendor and competitor longlists.

source_name: Prozorro.Sale — електронні торги активами банків, що ліквідуються (ФГВФО)
why_relevant: State e-auction system where the Deposit Guarantee Fund liquidates failed banks' assets — including equipment, vehicles, real estate and loan portfolios. Asset lots reveal what hardware and systems a bank actually owned, and who buys it; also a channel where vendors reacquire or resell installed base.

source_name: SmartTender.biz — майданчик державних і комерційних тендерів
why_relevant: Accredited Prozorro/Prozorro.Sale broker that ALSO hosts private commercial tenders, including auctions of bank property. Commercial tender boards are one of the few public windows onto private-sector (non-state bank) supplier selection, which Prozorro never covers.

source_name: Zakupivli24 / Zakupivli.Pro (PrivatBank procurement portal)
why_relevant: A tender/e-trading portal operated in PrivatBank's own ecosystem — a bank running a procurement marketplace. Directly exposes a major Ukrainian bank's own purchasing and the vendors bidding into it, and its Prozorro Market e-catalogue pages list software licences (e.g. Clarity) that banks and agencies buy.

source_name: data.gov.ua — Єдиний державний вебпортал відкритих даних
why_relevant: The upstream catalogue of Ukrainian open datasets that every aggregator resells, including registry dumps and contract lists. Enumerating its datasets identifies primary sources that can be collected directly and free of licence constraints instead of via paid intermediaries.

source_name: Радник у сфері публічних закупівель — каталог судових та інших реєстрів
why_relevant: Practitioner portal for Ukrainian procurement professionals that maintains curated tool/registry catalogues and republishes Clarity Project analyses. Its taxonomies enumerate further registries and analytical services relevant to contract tracing.

source_name: TAPAS / spendingToData — методичні рекомендації з публікації договорів
why_relevant: Documents the exact dataset schemas for 'Фінансова звітність' and 'Перелік укладених договорів' published via spending.gov.ua. Tells you which fields exist in contract disclosures and therefore what a supplier-mapping pipeline can actually extract.

source_name: ECEPP — EBRD Client E-Procurement Portal (notices, shortlists, contract awards)
why_relevant: Since 2019 all EBRD loan/grant-financed procurement, prequalification, shortlisting and contract-award notices for EBRD clients are published only on ECEPP. This is the single authoritative feed for Ukrainian bank and payment-infrastructure work financed by EBRD, including consultant selections that never reach Prozorro.

source_name: EBRD Technical Cooperation Project Summary Documents (TC PSD) — Ukraine financial sector
why_relevant: TC PSDs state the technical scope, beneficiary institution (e.g. NBU), consultant profile and indicative budget of donor-funded advisory assignments. Confirmed Ukraine-specific examples cover financial sector reform and a PMO at the National Bank of Ukraine supporting the Financial Sector Strategy — exactly the pre-procurement signal that precedes vendor selection.

source_name: EBRD project database (investment Project Summary Documents) — Ukraine financial institutions
why_relevant: Investment PSDs for Ukrainian banks (credit lines, risk-sharing, capital) disclose the accompanying technical-assistance components, which is where core-banking, digital channel and payments modernisation budgets sit. Also names the client banks, i.e. the buying institutions.

source_name: EBRD corporate procurement and consultancy services notices
why_relevant: Assignments contracted by the Bank itself (rather than by a client) — including sector studies and advisory work on Ukrainian financial infrastructure — appear here rather than on ECEPP. Complements ECEPP so the picture is not half-missing.

source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations — Ukraine procurement notices and contract awards
why_relevant: Publishes both procurement plans/notices and executed contract awards with supplier name, amount and date. Confirmed Ukrainian IT-vendor awards are visible here (e.g. computer equipment and EDMS licence awards to Ukrainian integrators), making this a direct vendor-identification route for World Bank-financed digital work.

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports — Ukraine Project Appraisal Documents (PAD)
why_relevant: PADs and implementation status reports set out the technical architecture, component budgets and procurement plan for financial-sector and public-financial-management IT projects — the level of scope detail commercial announcements never disclose. Historic Ukrainian precedent confirmed (State Tax Service Modernization PAD, Report 25875-UA).

source_name: IFC Disclosure Portal — Ukraine investment and advisory project disclosures
why_relevant: Reaches private Ukrainian banks that never appear in public procurement: confirmed disclosures for UKRSIBBANK, Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine and OTP Bank Ukraine risk-sharing facilities, each paired with an advisory component, plus advisory projects on credit reporting and digital financial services. Names the counterpart bank, the advisory scope and the timeline.
